title: X x_{Spec A} Spec(A/K) -> X is the closed immersion cut out by K O_X
statement: Let $A$ be a ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $f:X\to S$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For an ideal $K\subseteq A$ let $X_K=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with first projection $j_K:X_K\to X$, regard $X_K$ as a scheme over $S$ through $f\circ j_K$, and let $K\mathcal O_X\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be the image of $f^*\widetilde K\to f^*\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] ($\widetilde K\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ the ideal sheaf associated to $K$), and likewise $K\mathcal O_{X_K}$ for $X_K\to S$. (1) $j_K$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is $K\mathcal O_X$; for every affine open $U\subseteq X$, with $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$ (an $A$-algebra via $f$), $j_K^{-1}(U)$ is affine, $j_K^{-1}(U)\to U$ is identified over $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B/KB)\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ induced by the quotient map, and $(K\mathcal O_X)(U)=KB$. (2) For ideals $K,K'\subseteq A$, $(K\mathcal O_X)\cdot(K'\mathcal O_X)=(KK')\mathcal O_X$ (product of quasi-coherent ideal sheaves [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]); in particular $(K\mathcal O_X)^m=K^m\mathcal O_X$ for $m\ge1$. (3) Let $J\subseteq J'$ be ideals of $A$. The morphism $i:X_{J'}\to X_J$ with $j_J\circ i=j_{J'}$ whose composite with the second projection $X_J\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ is $X_{J'}\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/J')\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ (it exists and is unique by the universal property of $X_J$) is a closed immersion with ideal sheaf $J'\mathcal O_{X_J}$; over an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $X$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J'B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B/JB)$, induced by the quotient map. (4) For every ideal $L\subseteq A$, the image of $j_K^*(L\mathcal O_X)\to j_K^*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_{X_K}$ (the ideal $(L\mathcal O_X)\mathcal O_{X_K}$ of [def-nagata-extended-ideal] for $j_K$) equals $L\mathcal O_{X_K}$; over $j_K^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(B/KB)$ both are $L\cdot(B/KB)$.

proof.text: Compute the kernel of Spec(A/K) -> Spec A using Scheme.ker_of_isAffine, naturality of ΓSpecIso, invariance of a ring kernel under postcomposition by a ring isomorphism, and Ideal.mk_ker. This gives ofIdealTop(K.map ΓSpecIso.inv). The quotient map is surjective, hence its spectrum is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion]. Base change preserves closed immersions [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], and Mathlib ker_fst_of_isClosedImmersion identifies j_K.ker with that ideal sheaf pulled back along f.

For any ideal K and affine open U, apply the already proved ideal_comap_appLE [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension] with the top affine open of Spec A. ofIdealTop_ideal and Ideal.map_map identify the result with the extension of K along ΓSpecIso.inv followed by f.appLE. This computes (K O_X)(U)=KB without any module-pullback or tilde theorem.

For a closed immersion j and an affine open U, its inverse image is affine [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion]. Apply Mathlib IsClosedImmersion.Spec_iff to (j restricted to U) followed by U.isoSpec.hom to obtain a quotient by an ideal I. Compute the kernel of this quotient using step 1 and ker_comp_of_isIso. Compute the same kernel from the restriction appTop formula and isoSpec_hom_appTop: after cancelling topIso, it is the comap of j.ker.ideal U along ΓSpecIso.hom. Since that ring map is surjective, Ideal.comap_injective_of_surjective gives I=j.ker.ideal U. Substituting the ideal yields the required isomorphism and projection identity. For j_K, steps 1 and 2 identify this ideal with KB, completing clause (1).

proof.text: Use step 2 for K, K-prime, their product and their powers. IdealSheafData.ext reduces equality of ideal sheaves to equality of ideals on each affine open. ideal_mul and ideal_pow [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], together with Ideal.map_mul and Ideal.map_pow, prove clause (2).

For J <= J-prime, let c be Spec of Ideal.Quotient.factor h. Functoriality and factor_comp_mk give c followed by the quotient immersion for J equal to the quotient immersion for J-prime. Construct i by pullback.lift with first projection j_J-prime and second projection p_J-prime followed by c; pullback.lift_fst, lift_snd and hom_ext give both identities and uniqueness. As i followed by j_J equals j_J-prime, i is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-factor-ideal-inclusion]. For its kernel, use Hom.ker_comp to write j_J-prime.ker = i.ker.map j_J. Pulling back this pushforward along the monomorphism j_J recovers i.ker: the identity square with i.ker.subschemeι and its composite with j_J is cartesian by of_horiz_isIso_mono, and ker_fst_of_isClosedImmersion, the pullback isomorphism, and ker_subschemeι prove the assertion. This is the already proved library lemma comap_map_of_isClosedImmersion. Step 1 and comap_comp then identify i.ker with J-prime O_X_J.

Choose the quotient isomorphisms of clause (1) for J and J-prime. To prove compatibility of i with the spectrum of the quotient factor, compose the desired identity with j_J, which is a monomorphism. The projection identities of the charts and i reduce both sides to the quotient map B -> B/J-prime B followed by the affine inclusion. The remaining equality is factor_comp_mk and functoriality of Spec. Cancel j_J to obtain the displayed equality, completing clause (3).

For clause (4), apply Mathlib IdealSheafData.comap_comp to the ideal attached to L, j_K and f. For the affine formula choose the affine inverse image supplied by the closed immersion. Apply ideal_comap_appLE [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension] to j_K and U with its full preimage, where appLE is app. Step 2 computes the starting ideal LB. The composition identity gives the same formula for the other ideal. No closed-immersion pushforward module theorem is required.
